title: Where the boat musicians lived in St. Louis
summary: Russell asks if the men took rooms in St. Louis; Desvigne says nobody lived on the boat except when travelling upriver.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: One other question while I interrupt you, Fats. Did most of the fellas have rooms then in St. Louis?
Well, coming down on the boat, we had our rooms.
I don't know. But most of them, would they live on the boat, or would they sleep in St. Louis? Yeah.
Well, they had permission to sleep on a boat too, and a boat was here, you see, but they'd go out in town and get a room. No, but he said St. Louis.
And St. Louis too, I wonder.

No, when you said, when I stayed in St. Louis, I think it was three or four summers that I went, I worked with Faith Marlborough's Band, when I had my room out in town. No one stayed on the boat in St. Louis, they operated out there.
No one stayed on the boat.

The only thing I ever stayed on the boat there was the deckhands, I imagine. That was all. But nobody lived on the boat. Only when you go up the river. That's right. When you're traveling down from St. Louis, you know, you're... That's right.
